keys.meta_title: Eye Test Online: Free Visual Acuity Test for Each Eye | CoreSkillAI
keys.meta_desc: Free online eye test for distance vision. Calibrate your screen with a bank card, then read tumbling E letters from 3 metres to get a logMAR and Snellen score for each eye. About 5 minutes.
keys.vis_desc: Calibrate your screen with a bank card and read letters from 3 metres. Get a logMAR and Snellen score for each eye.
keys.vis_how1: You need a bank card or any card of the same size, a tape measure, and a laptop or desktop screen.
keys.vis_how2: First you match a rectangle on screen to your card, so the letters are drawn at their true size.
keys.vis_how3: Then you stand 3 metres from the screen, cover one eye and say which way each letter E points. A helper or a wireless keyboard makes this easy.
keys.vis_how4: If you wear glasses for distance, keep them on. Takes about 5 minutes. This is a screening for curiosity, not an eye examination.
keys.vis_start_desc: Measures how small a letter each eye can read from a known distance, with the same chart principles eye clinics use.
keys.vis_cal1: Hold a bank card flat against the screen, at the top-left corner of the grey rectangle. Change the size until the rectangle is exactly as wide as the card.
keys.vis_cal2: Any card of this size works: a debit or credit card, a driving licence or an ID card. Do not use a business card.
keys.vis_dist1: Measure the distance from the screen to your eyes with a tape measure. 3 metres is best. Stand, or sit, with your eyes level with the screen.
keys.vis_dist2: At 3 metres the letters a person with normal vision can just read are about 4 mm tall. Turn the screen brightness up and avoid glare on the screen.
keys.vis_nofit: This screen is too small to draw the chart at this distance. Use a laptop or desktop screen, or choose a shorter distance.
keys.vis_cover1: Cover the other eye with the palm of your hand without pressing on it. Keep both eyes open behind your hand.
keys.vis_keys: For each letter E, say or press which way its open side points: right, down, left or up. If you cannot tell, guess.
keys.vis_keyhint: Arrow keys work too. The red bar marks the current letter.
keys.vis_v_worse: Could not read the largest line this screen can show. Have your eyes examined.
keys.vis_v_good: Normal or better than normal for distance (6/6 or 20/20, or better).
keys.vis_v_mild: Below 6/6 but within the range not counted as vision impairment (6/12 or better).
keys.vis_v_imp1: In the range the WHO classification calls mild vision impairment.
keys.vis_v_imp2: In the range the WHO classification calls moderate vision impairment or worse.
keys.vis_floor: You read the smallest line this screen can draw, so your vision may be even better.
keys.vis_diff: Your two eyes differ by two lines or more. That is worth checking with an optometrist or ophthalmologist, especially if it is new.
keys.vis_how_read: logMAR 0.0 equals 6/6 (20/20). Each 0.1 is one line on a clinical chart; lower numbers mean sharper vision.
keys.vis_disclaimer: A home screen test can differ from a clinic chart by a line or more, and it does not check eye health, near vision, colour vision or the visual field. It cannot be used for a driving licence. Sudden loss or blurring of vision is an emergency: see a doctor the same day.
